title: A Yearbook for the Locker
premise: Rafael Kavanagh has spent four years at Hollow Creek High perfecting the art of being unnoticed, counting down to graduation from a town where he is the only out kid. When the school's legendary ghost begins leaving him notes in ink that vanishes by morning — notes that know things no living person should — Rafael is pulled into a decades-old injustice: a student erased from every yearbook after being outed in 1979. As Rafael investigates with an unlikely found family of misfits, he discovers the ghost's 'impossible ink' has a human source, and that winning the state debate championship — and auditioning for the spring musical he's always been too afraid to try out for — are both part of finishing what the ghost started: putting a name back on the record. The story ends with Rafael publicly claiming his own name at graduation, the restored yearbook page unveiled, and the 'ghost' revealed as the elderly former janitor who loved the erased boy and never stopped waiting for someone to ask.
about_author: Ines Underhill is the pen name of a former small-town debate coach who grew up as one of three out teenagers in a farming county and never forgot what the trophy case chose to remember. They write stories about kids who refuse to be footnotes.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Lockers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Establishes Hollow Creek, his invisibility strategy, and his countdown calendar taped inside locker 214. A cruel anonymous note reminds him why he hides. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety, ending when he finds the first impossible note — his full name, in ink that fades before homeroom.

chapters.title: The Ghost of Room 12
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He researches the school ghost legend and learns it centers on a student who vanished from records in 1979. The second note appears, quoting something Rafael said aloud only in the empty auditorium. Emotional beat: fear curdling into fascination — someone sees him, and isn't mocking him.

chapters.title: Debate Club Has One Chair Left
chapters.summary: Dahlia Okafor's POV. The sharp-tongued new girl recruits Rafael for the dying debate team because she needs a partner and he 'argues beautifully in his head.' Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Rafael realizes Dahlia is also performing a version of herself, and their partnership cracks his isolation open.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Testing the notes against chemistry class reagents, he confirms the ink is handmade iron-gall — old-fashioned, deliberate. A third note names the erased student: Elias Marsh. Emotional beat: the mystery becomes personal; Rafael recognizes a boy who was made invisible exactly like him.

chapters.title: What the Trophy Case Forgot
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with flashbacks to 1979 through Elias's recovered journal pages. Rafael and Dahlia find the gap in the yearbook archive — a razor-bladed page. Emotional beat: grief and fury; justice outside the law starts here, because the school will never fix this voluntarily.

chapters.title: The Audition Nobody Expected
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. On a dare from Dahlia and theater kid Marcus, Rafael auditions for the spring musical — and gets a lead, detonating his invisibility plan. Rumors spread; his mother finds the notes. Emotional beat: terror of exposure colliding with the first taste of wanting to be seen.

chapters.title: Detention with Mr. Voss
chapters.summary: Mr. Voss's POV, the elderly janitor. We learn he mixed the ink, left the notes, and has guarded Elias's memory for forty-five years. Watching Rafael, he wonders if passing the burden on is mercy or cowardice. Emotional beat: tender, guilt-ridden; the 'ghost' is a man who stayed when everyone else looked away.

chapters.title: Regionals, and the Threat
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The team reaches regionals, but a school board member threatens to cancel the musical and expel the 'instigators' digging into old records. Rafael must choose between safety and the truth. Emotional beat: rising dread; the cost of visibility arrives all at once, and Rafael refuses to fold.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Rafael and Dahlia win the state debate final using Elias's own words from the journal as their evidence — arguing, on stage, that a record deliberately falsified is a wrong the town still owes. Emotional beat: triumph braided with defiance; the crowd hears the name Elias Marsh for the first time in decades.

chapters.title: A Yearbook for the Locker
chapters.summary: Resolution. At the final performance and then graduation, Mr. Voss comes forward; the school restores Elias's page, and Rafael delivers the valedictory address with his name spoken plainly, proudly. Locker 214 holds a new yearbook — Elias's story bound beside his own. Emotional beat: found family, claimed identity, justice finally on the record.
